title: Trump Expresses Interest in Meeting Kim Jong-un 'As Early As This Month' During Beijing Visit
detail: During US President Trump's state visit to Beijing (May 12–15, 2026), South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo reported that Trump told him he 'could meet Kim Jong-un as early as this month.' No meeting had been confirmed by May 13. Trump's comment came on the sidelines of his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, where Korean Peninsula stability was a secondary agenda item. North Korea was not a primary focus of the Trump-Xi talks, which centered on trade and Taiwan. NK News and South Korean officials noted that any Trump-Kim summit would likely require preliminary talks at the working level — a step that has not occurred. Trump previously held summits with Kim in Singapore (June 2018) and Hanoi (February 2019), both of which produced no denuclearization agreement. Kim's recent signal of openness to talks — conditional on the US dropping its denuclearization precondition — appears to have opened diplomatic space.

media.caption: Trump says he could meet Kim Jong Un as early as this month, per South Korea's prime minister

title: AEI Analysis: Kim Jong-un Actively Consolidating Independent Cult of Personality Distinct From Predecessors
detail: The American Enterprise Institute's Korean Peninsula Update for May 12, 2026 assessed that Kim Jong-un is systematically constructing an independent cult of personality distinct from the legacies of Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il. Analysts noted Kim increasingly presents himself as a transformative military-modernization leader — the man who completed the nuclear deterrent, built a blue-water navy, deployed troops abroad, and achieved a strategic partnership with Russia — rather than simply inheriting the Kim dynasty's revolutionary credentials. The AEI analysis also noted DPRK's revised constitution (confirmed May 6) and the Victory Day parade participation (May 9) as evidence of a deliberate DPRK repositioning from a defensive state isolated by sanctions to an active military partner in the Russia-led anti-Western order. The FDD separately published analysis on May 7 noting that Russian security transfers to North Korea (including advanced missile and space technology) are creating strategic complications for China, which now faces a more capable and less dependent DPRK on its border.

media.caption: AEI analysis: Kim Jong-un building independent leadership legacy distinct from his predecessors
